headline: SpaceX faces scrutiny. True Anomaly raises cash.
deck: Concerns grow over SpaceX's rideshare program and new funding rounds signal shifting priorities.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M amid defense demand
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190M in a Series C round, valuing the co-orbital security firm at $1.6B. This funding underscores the Department of Defense's growing reliance on commercial capabilities for space domain awareness. With defense budgets tightening, the spotlight is on companies that can deliver tangible results.
stories.soWhat: In an industry where cash flow is king, True Anomaly's success highlights that the DoD is willing to pay for security solutions, even if they come with a hefty price tag.

stories.head: SpaceX's rideshare program faces existential questions
stories.body: SpaceX launched Transporter-17, but concerns about the viability of its rideshare program are mounting. Rivals are increasingly vocal about the competitive landscape, suggesting that SpaceX's dominance might be more precarious than previously thought. The Pentagon's commitment to competition could further complicate SpaceX's future plans.
stories.soWhat: When competitors start circling like vultures, it’s a clear sign that the rideshare gravy train might be hitting some bumps in the road.

stories.head: Isar Aerospace lands Canadian launch site deal
stories.body: Isar Aerospace has signed an agreement to develop a launch site in Canada, linked to a submarine sale to the Canadian military. This move expands their operational footprint and aligns with increasing defense spending in the region. With a focus on their Spectrum rocket, Isar is positioning itself as a key player in North American space launches.
stories.soWhat: If the Canadian military is putting money into submarines, Isar's launch site could become a strategic asset in a rapidly evolving defense landscape.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's next moves
watchlist.body: With mounting scrutiny, how SpaceX adapts its rideshare strategy could set the tone for the entire market.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's next steps post-funding
watchlist.body: The new capital infusion will be telling; watch for how True Anomaly scales its operations to meet DoD demands.

watchlist.title: Isar Aerospace's Canadian operations
watchlist.body: As Isar develops its launch site, the implications for North American launch capabilities will be worth monitoring.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
